concerns_addressed: Enabled webhooks require a valid raw-body HMAC or configured verification token; the previous verify_signature=false bypass is not honored (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppService.php:19-31,107-131).

Failed inbound events remain retryable and provider-derived order idempotency prevents duplicate orders (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppService.php:67-95; apps/api/app/Services/OrderCreationService.php:20-81).

Outlet phones are canonicalized and uniquely indexed, while sender resolution rejects multiple active matches including legacy raw-phone conflicts (apps/api/app/Models/Outlet.php:46-67; apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppSenderResolver.php:10-28; apps/api/database/migrations/2026_09_08_000015_add_canonical_phone_to_outlets.php:11-46).
Structured payloads require a non-empty list, positive integer quantities, resolvable products, and distinct resolved product IDs (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppPayloadParser.php:53-74).

Notifications are Confirmed-only and provider failures are isolated from the already-committed order/payment state (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppOutboundService.php:19-26; apps/api/app/Http/Controllers/WhatsAppController.php:65-83; apps/api/app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php:145-158).

Outbound notifications have a unique logical key, stable provider idempotency key, and the production HTTP client sends that key on text delivery/retry (apps/api/database/migrations/2026_09_08_000016_add_notification_idempotency_to_whatsapp_messages.php:11-15; apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppOutboundService.php:28-46,139-177; apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppHttpClient.php:21-29,50-56).

Inbound and outbound races now use insertOrIgnore followed by lockForUpdate within a usable transaction, rather than catching a PostgreSQL unique violation and querying an aborted transaction (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppService.php:134-163; apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppOutboundService.php:28-55).

Outbound sending rows have a claimed_at lease, fresh-lease protection, stale-lease reclaim, and cleanup on success/failure; retries reuse the stable provider key (apps/api/app/Services/WhatsAppOutboundService.php:113-158; apps/api/database/migrations/2026_09_09_000017_add_claimed_at_to_whatsapp_messages.php:9-14).

WhatsApp responsibilities remain separated across the webhook service, payload parser, sender resolver, outbound service, and provider client; no former mixed-responsibility service regression was found.

strengths: The Laravel PostgreSQL grammar compiles insertOrIgnore to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the subsequent SELECT ... FOR UPDATE waits for and locks the committed winner, so neither conflict path queries an aborted transaction (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Query/Grammars/PostgresGrammar.php:353-356; WhatsAppService.php:142-163; WhatsAppOutboundService.php:36-55).

Outbound creation and delivery have clear transaction boundaries: logical-row convergence is locked before commit, then claimed_at is acquired under a row lock before the provider call; fresh leases are not duplicated and stale leases are reclaimable with the stable provider key.
The lease migration adds the nullable claim timestamp and a delivery index; success and failure paths clear the claim and persist attempts/error state.
Focused WhatsAppTest passes with 11 tests and 49 assertions, including fresh/stale lease behavior, provider failure isolation, strict payloads, sender ambiguity, and Confirmed-only notifications.
The full API suite passes with 70 tests and 408 assertions.

issues.description: The optional PostgreSQL concurrency suite is explicit and correctly skips when DB_CONNECTION=pgsql/pdo_pgsql or the test database is unavailable. This environment has no pdo_pgsql and the Docker daemon is unavailable, so the two real PostgreSQL worker races could not be executed here; SQL grammar, transaction/lock flow, and test setup were inspected and are sound.
